A 29-year-old male seeks medical attention for progressive difficulty swallowing that began several
weeks ago, affecting both solids and liquids. His medical history is unremarkable except for recent
travel to South America. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure
113/66 mmHg, heart rate 99/min, respiratory rate 17/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Head, ears, eyes, nose, and throat examination is normal, and abdominal examination reveals no
masses. What should be the initial step in management? Answer Choices: (A) CT scan of the chest (B)
Empiric proton pump inhibitor therapy (C) Trial of dietary modification (D) Upper gastrointestinal series
(E) Capsule endoscopy (F) Esophageal pH monitoring (G) Manometry (H) Barium swallow (I) Chest
X-ray (J) Endoscopy
 A. Endoscopy
B. Manometry
C. Capsule endoscopy
D. Barium swallow
E. CT scan of the chest
F. Empiric proton pump inhibitor therapy
G. Trial of dietary modification
H. Upper gastrointestinal series
I. Esophageal pH monitoring
J. Chest X-ray
